memories.content: June: prefers turning architecture debates into one small reversible prototype before discussing a larger programme.
June: a dashboard review exposed that a green status card was based on stale data, so freshness became part of every readiness check.
July: found that technical workshops work best when the group starts with one real failure path rather than a feature tour.
July: is shaping a fictional retail data platform demo around portable data, typed restoration and visible reconciliation.
August: prefers executive updates that state the tension first, show evidence second and finish with a measurable decision.
August: the next demo rehearsal should prove continuity across chats without using any real customer or colleague information.
June: prefers concise explanations that end with the exact command or check needed to verify the claim.
June: noticed that busy status meetings improve when each claim includes its source and the time it was last refreshed.
July: likes demos with a visible before-and-after moment rather than a long sequence of setup screens.
July: is preparing a fictional operations review where an apparently healthy dashboard conceals an old data snapshot.
August: prefers risks to be named plainly and paired with one practical mitigation instead of a dense risk register.
August: wants the shared learning demo to show useful human experience surviving beyond one model response and one user session.

wisdom.text: A green status without a fresh timestamp is decoration, not evidence.
